program.title: Year Long Evidence Based & Clinical Course in Implant Dentistry
program.subtitle: Evidence Based & Clinical Implant Dentistry
details: Evidence-based teaching plus practical clinical training
Training on patients provided by the course under direct mentoring at no extra cost
description: The BAIRD Evidence Based & Clinical Course in Implant Dentistry is one of the most successful private courses in implant dentistry in the United Kingdom.
It is designed to give participants sound grounding knowledge in implant dentistry as well as practical training on patients provided by the course.
Past graduates are already placing and restoring implants with confidence in their own dental practices.
faculty: Dr Hassan Maghaireh — Chairman of BAIRD Academy; ITI Fellow and Speaker.
Prof Marco Esposito — Professor of Evidence-Based Medicine and Dentistry at Vita-Salute San Raffaele University, Milan; editor and author with Cochrane Collaboration.
Prof StJohn Crean — Consultant in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Vice-Chancellor of The University of Central Lancashire.
Prof Crawford Bain — Specialist Certificates in Periodontics and Fixed Prosthodontics; former Senior Lecturer and MSc Coordinator in Dental Primary Care at The University of Glasgow.
Prof Ziad Al-Ani — Senior Lecturer at the School of Medicine, Dentistry and Nursing, University of Glasgow.
Dr Kasim Butt — Consultant and Specialist in Restorative Dentistry at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust; Head of the Scientific Committee at BAIRD Academy.
Prof Domniki Chatzopoulou — Professor of Periodontology, Specialist Periodontist, Reader, and Postgraduate Course Director for the DClinDent in Periodontology at Queen Mary University of London.
Dr Victoria Ivancheva — Young ITI Ambassador; member of the Scientific Committee and Head of the Mentoring Committee at BAIRD Academy.
Dr Sarra Jawad — Restorative Consultant at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust.

Dr Lee Feinberg — Specialist in Dental and Maxillofacial Radiology; Consultant Dental and Maxillofacial Radiologist at King's College Hospital and Eastman Dental Hospital, part of University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.
Dr Aziz Ghanem Aziz — Clinical Lecturer in Implant Dentistry at Eastman; examiner at The RCS Edinburgh Implant Membership exam; implant dentist in Cardiff.
Dr Koray Keran — Clinical Director and Principal Dental Surgeon at The London Centre for Implant & Aesthetic Dentistry.
Dr Chia Yeoh — Implant and Cosmetic Dentist at Perfect 32.

modules.title: Module 1
modules.topics: Introduction into Implant Dentistry, Success Criteria, Pink aesthetics and Treatment Planning.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Core implant foundations: history, bone biology, surgical principles, biomechanics, restorative thinking and complications.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Foundations, History and Bone Biology
lectures.copy: Introduces the biological and historical foundations of implant dentistry, including osseointegration, bone behaviour and the principles that underpin predictable treatment.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Foundations, History and Bone Biology
materials.summary: Builds the essential context for implant dentistry, from early development through to bone healing, implant integration and the biological basis for clinical success.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Foundations, History and Bone Biology
materials.summary: Checks understanding of osseointegration, bone biology, key historical milestones and the foundational terminology used throughout the course.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Surgical Principles and Biomechanics
lectures.copy: Connects implant surgery with load, stability and force management so learners can understand why implant position, angulation and prosthetic design matter.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Surgical Principles and Biomechanics
materials.summary: Covers core surgical concepts, implant stability, force distribution and the biomechanical decisions that influence long-term implant outcomes.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Surgical Principles and Biomechanics
materials.summary: Tests surgical sequencing, biomechanical reasoning, implant stability concepts and the clinical implications of force control.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Restoration, Complications and Clinical Excellence
lectures.copy: Brings the first day together by linking restorative planning, complication awareness and professional judgement in implant care.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Restoration, Complications and Clinical Excellence
materials.summary: Explores restoration-led planning, common complications, clinical decision-making and the standards expected in high-quality implant dentistry.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Restoration, Complications and Clinical Excellence
materials.summary: Reviews restorative planning, complication recognition, treatment priorities and the clinical excellence themes from the lecture.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Restorative planning day focused on removable options, adhesive bridges and choosing implant dimensions and positions responsibly.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Mastering Partial Dentures
lectures.copy: Reviews partial denture design and decision-making so learners can compare conventional and implant-based solutions with confidence.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Mastering Partial Dentures
materials.summary: Explains the role of partial dentures in treatment planning, including design principles, patient suitability and when removable options remain appropriate.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Partial Dentures
materials.summary: Reinforces key partial denture concepts, design choices, indications and limitations in the context of implant treatment planning.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Resin Bonded Bridges
lectures.copy: Covers resin bonded bridges as a conservative fixed option, including case selection, design and risk factors for failure.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Resin Bonded Bridges
materials.summary: Outlines indications, contraindications, preparation principles and clinical design considerations for predictable resin bonded bridges.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Resin Bonded Bridges
materials.summary: Assesses bridge design, abutment selection, bonding principles and factors that affect survival of resin bonded restorations.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Implant Size and Position
lectures.copy: Focuses on choosing implant size and position from a prosthetically driven plan while respecting anatomy, aesthetics and bone volume.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Implant Size and Position
materials.summary: Covers implant diameter, length, spacing, angulation and restorative emergence considerations for safe and aesthetic placement.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Implant Size and Position
materials.summary: Tests implant sizing, spacing, anatomical clearance and prosthetic positioning principles from the lecture.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Surgical preparation day covering local anaesthesia, patient readiness, equipment handling and the practical implant placement sequence.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Local Anaesthesia and Patient Preparation
lectures.copy: Sets out how to prepare the patient, team and surgical environment before implant placement, with emphasis on comfort and safety.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Local Anaesthesia and Patient Preparation
materials.summary: Covers anaesthetic planning, patient preparation, consent checks, asepsis and team coordination before implant surgery.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Anaesthesia, Preparation and Team
materials.summary: Reviews patient preparation, local anaesthetic considerations, surgical setup and the team roles needed for a controlled implant procedure.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Instruments and Surgical Motor
lectures.copy: Introduces the surgical kit, motor settings and instrument workflow used during implant placement.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Instruments and Surgical Motor
materials.summary: Explains implant instruments, handpiece and motor setup, torque and speed awareness, irrigation and efficient surgical workflow.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Instruments and Surgical Motor
materials.summary: Checks recognition of instruments, motor settings, surgical sequencing and safe handling principles.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Drilling Sequence and Implant Placement
lectures.copy: Walks through osteotomy preparation and implant insertion, linking drill choice to bone density and primary stability.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Drilling Sequence and Implant Placement
materials.summary: Details the step-by-step drilling sequence, depth control, cortical management, insertion torque and practical placement decisions.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Drilling Sequence and Implant Placement
materials.summary: Tests drill sequence decisions, implant bed preparation, bone-density adjustments and placement principles.

modules.title: Oral Surgery Mastery
modules.topics: Additional standalone weekend covering foundations of oral surgery, local anaesthetic mastery and wisdom teeth complications.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Focused oral surgery study day covering surgical foundations, local anaesthetic delivery and wisdom tooth complications.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Foundations of Oral Surgery
lectures.copy: Introduces the clinical principles, assessment habits and operative discipline needed for safe oral surgery.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Foundations of Oral Surgery
materials.summary: Covers core oral surgery foundations, including assessment, surgical judgement, patient communication and safe operative planning.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Local Anaesthetic Mastery
lectures.copy: Develops a more precise approach to local anaesthetic choice, delivery and troubleshooting in oral surgery.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Local Anaesthetic Mastery
materials.summary: Explains anaesthetic techniques, anatomical targets, common failures and practical strategies for reliable pain control.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Wisdom Teeth and Complications
lectures.copy: Reviews wisdom tooth assessment and the prevention, recognition and management of surgical complications.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Wisdom Teeth and Complications
materials.summary: Covers third molar planning, risk assessment, consent issues and complication management for wisdom tooth surgery.

modules.title: Module 2
modules.topics: Cone Beam CT Scan Training, Surgical Planning for Implant Cases and Surgical Principles in Implant Dentistry.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Patient selection and stabilisation day, moving from treatment planning foundations into PECOFA and whole-case risk assessment.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Patient Selection and Treatment Planning Foundations
lectures.copy: Frames implant treatment around patient suitability, expectations, medical and social risk, and restoratively driven outcomes.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Patient Selection and Treatment Planning Foundations
materials.summary: Covers patient assessment, eligibility, expectations, risk factors, denture experience and the principle that the final teeth drive implant planning.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Patient Selection and Planning
materials.summary: Tests patient selection, compliance, smoking and medical risk, prosthetic planning and expectation management.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · PECOFA Stabilisation Framework
lectures.copy: Uses PECOFA to sequence stabilisation logically before definitive implant or restorative treatment begins.

materials.label: Lecture 2: PECOFA Stabilisation Framework
materials.summary: Explains periodontal, endodontic, coronal, occlusal, functional and aesthetic sequencing, including how to stabilise forwards and plan backwards.

materials.label: Quiz 2: PECOFA Stabilisation Framework
materials.summary: Checks PECOFA order, periodontal stability, endodontic prognosis, ferrule, cuspal coverage and restorative sequencing.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Whole-Case Planning and High-Risk Patients
lectures.copy: Brings risk assessment, consent and treatment sequencing together for complex or higher-risk implant patients.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Whole-Case Planning and High-Risk Patients
materials.summary: Covers whole-mouth diagnosis, problem lists, red flags, medication and periodontal risk, consent documentation and avoiding unsuitable cases.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Whole-Case Planning, Risk and Litigation
materials.summary: Assesses medication risks, periodontal history, documentation, consent, aesthetic risk and case-selection judgement.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Consent and medico-legal reasoning day covering valid consent, best interests, case law, coercion and ethical refusal of treatment.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Consent, Best Interests and Refusal
lectures.copy: Explains what makes consent valid, how to approach capacity and best interests, and how to document difficult refusal scenarios.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Consent, Best Interests and Refusal
materials.summary: Covers capacity, information, voluntariness, carers and legal guardians, safeguarding, confidentiality and defensible documentation.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Consent, Case Law and Practical Application
materials.summary: Tests foundational consent principles, best-interests decisions, documentation habits and practical medico-legal application.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Advanced Consent Scenarios
lectures.copy: Develops consent judgement through nuanced clinical scenarios, case facts and decision-making under uncertainty.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Advanced Consent Scenarios
materials.summary: Explores detailed consent cases, clinical risk disclosure, patient-specific material risks and communication that stands up to scrutiny.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Advanced Consent Scenarios
materials.summary: Uses detailed case questions to check deeper understanding of consent, clinical anatomy, risk disclosure and patient-centred judgement.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Coercion, Practical Consent and Refusing Treatment
lectures.copy: Focuses on coercion, cooling-off time, treatment refusal, local anaesthetic consent and implant timing discussions.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Coercion, Practical Consent and Refusing Treatment
materials.summary: Covers coercive pressure, ethical sales boundaries, refusing inappropriate treatment, additional-treatment consent and immediate versus delayed implant decisions.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Integration and Application
materials.summary: Tests cross-lecture links, practical refusal scenarios, coercion, local anaesthetic consent and scenario-based clinical judgement.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: CBCT training day covering scan physics, dose and justification, reporting scope, anatomy and clinical case interpretation.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · CBCT Fundamentals: Training, Scope and Physics
lectures.copy: Introduces CBCT training requirements, imaging scope, scanner principles, field of view, voxels and the limits of 3D imaging.

materials.label: Lecture 1: CBCT Fundamentals, Training, Scope and Physics
materials.summary: Covers CBCT training tiers, IRMER expectations, scanner mechanics, field of view, voxel size, dose-quality trade-offs and when 2D imaging falls short.

materials.label: Quiz 1: CBCT Fundamentals
materials.summary: Checks CBCT physics, reporting scope, field-of-view choices, voxel concepts and basic image-orientation principles.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Dose, Risk, Justification and Guidelines
lectures.copy: Explains radiation dose, patient risk, justification and how to select CBCT only when it changes diagnosis or management.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Dose, Risk, Justification and Guidelines
materials.summary: Covers effective dose, age-related risk, patient communication, pregnancy enquiries, CBCT selection guidelines and field-of-view justification.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Dose, Risk and Justification
materials.summary: Tests dose comparisons, stochastic risk, justification rules, patient communication and appropriate CBCT selection.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · CBCT Anatomy and Clinical Cases
lectures.copy: Applies CBCT interpretation to mandibular and maxillary anatomy, sinus findings, artefacts and clinically relevant case patterns.

materials.label: Lecture 3: CBCT Anatomy and Clinical Cases
materials.summary: Reviews ID canal anatomy, anterior loops, lingual canals, sinus anatomy, pathology, artefacts and a practical approach to reading scans.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Anatomy and Clinical Cases
materials.summary: Assesses anatomical recognition, sinus and nerve risk, artefact interpretation and clinical case judgement from CBCT images.

modules.title: Module 3
modules.topics: Risk Analysis, Periodontal Management, Bone Grafting Principles, Socket Grafting and Patient Selection in Implant Dentistry.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Soft tissue and flap design day covering peri-implant tissue biology, grafting decisions, surgical access and anatomy-led flap planning.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Soft Tissue Fundamentals in Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Introduces the peri-implant soft tissue seal, keratinised mucosa, tissue thickness and why soft tissue quality matters for long-term implant stability.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Soft Tissue Fundamentals in Implant Dentistry
materials.summary: Covers the biological foundations of peri-implant soft tissue, including mucosal health, keratinised tissue, tissue thickness and the clinical signs of stability.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Soft Tissue Fundamentals
materials.summary: Checks understanding of peri-implant tissue anatomy, health indicators, keratinised mucosa and soft tissue risk factors.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Soft Tissue Management and Grafting
lectures.copy: Explains how to assess tissue deficiencies and select soft tissue management or grafting approaches to improve function, health and aesthetics.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Soft Tissue Management and Grafting
materials.summary: Reviews soft tissue augmentation principles, grafting indications, timing, recipient-site preparation and practical management around implants.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Soft Tissue Management and Grafting
materials.summary: Tests grafting indications, tissue-management choices, timing decisions and the clinical reasoning behind soft tissue augmentation.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Flap Design and Surgical Decision-Making
lectures.copy: Covers flap design choices, access, blood supply and closure principles so surgical exposure supports healing rather than compromising it.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Flap Design and Surgical Decision-Making
materials.summary: Explains incision planning, flap elevation, release, visibility, blood supply preservation and choosing the right access for each implant scenario.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Flap Design and Decision-Making
materials.summary: Assesses flap design principles, incision placement, access decisions, closure strategy and surgical risk judgement.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Bone management day covering post-extraction biology, digital planning, GBR materials, membranes, sinus grafting, socket grafting and staged reconstruction.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Post-Extraction Biology and Treatment Planning
lectures.copy: Explains what happens to bone after extraction and how timing, digital planning, socket position, implant placement and grafting choices shape the treatment journey.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Post-Extraction Biology and Treatment Planning
materials.summary: Covers bundle bone theory, post-extraction bone loss, timing protocols, surgical guides, implant positioning, primary stability and simultaneous versus staged GBR decisions.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Post-Extraction Biology and Treatment Planning
materials.summary: Tests extraction-site biology, timing choices, digital planning, implant positioning, torque thresholds and early grafting decisions.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · GBR Principles, Materials and Membranes
lectures.copy: Builds the guided bone regeneration framework from defect classification through graft-material selection, membrane choice, stabilisation and healing.

materials.label: Lecture 2: GBR Principles, Materials and Membranes
materials.summary: Reviews the 2 mm rule, defect classification, autogenous bone, allograft, xenograft, layering techniques, membranes, decortication and causes of GBR failure.

materials.label: Quiz 2: GBR Materials and Membranes
materials.summary: Checks GBR principles, graft-material selection, membrane properties, stabilisation, healing timelines and decision-making for guided regeneration.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Sinus, Socket and Staged Bone Grafting
lectures.copy: Applies bone management principles to sinus augmentation, socket preservation and staged grafting for more complex implant sites.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Sinus, Socket and Staged Bone Grafting
materials.summary: Covers sinus anatomy, internal and external sinus grafting, socket graft material choice, staged block grafting, healing timelines and prosthetically led complex planning.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Sinus, Socket and Staged Grafting
materials.summary: Assesses sinus grafting decisions, socket preservation, staged graft indications, material selection and complex bone-management planning.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Advanced implant planning day covering intelligent bone augmentation, GBR and socket grafting protocols, and orthodontic aligner planning around implants.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Intelligent Bone Grafting
lectures.copy: Explores modern augmentation choices, from CAD-CAM bone blocks and allografts to membrane selection, flap design and staged GBR protocols.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Intelligent Bone Grafting
materials.summary: Covers patient-centred augmentation planning, allograft and autogenous options, CAD-CAM blocks, sausage technique, magnesium membranes, flap design and kit setup.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Bone Grafting and Augmentation
materials.summary: Tests modern bone grafting concepts, augmentation material choices, membrane selection, staged protocols and clinical planning decisions.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · GBR and Socket Grafting
lectures.copy: Focuses on GBR principles, socket grafting, ridge preservation and the protocols that protect ridge volume after extraction.

materials.label: Lecture 2: GBR and Socket Grafting
materials.summary: Reviews tissue-level versus bone-level implants, GBR membrane fixation, socket grafting steps, ridge preservation, Kahn classification and post-operative protocols.

materials.label: Quiz 2: GBR and Socket Grafting
materials.summary: Checks GBR requirements, socket grafting sequence, ridge preservation indications, membrane choices and failure prevention.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Aligners and Implant Planning
lectures.copy: Shows how orthodontic aligners and implant planning work together to create space, manage roots and improve multidisciplinary outcomes.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Aligners and Implant Planning
materials.summary: Covers orthodontics before implants, space and root-position requirements, aligner mechanics, TADs, retention, digital collaboration and combined treatment sequencing.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Aligners and Implant Planning
materials.summary: Assesses implant space planning, orthodontic sequencing, aligner mechanics, root-position management and multidisciplinary treatment decisions.

modules.title: Module 4
modules.topics: Bone and Soft Tissue Healing Principles in Implant Dentistry, Medical Problems in Dentistry and Dental Implant Photography.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Evidence-led implant decision-making day covering critical appraisal, peri-implant disease and the clinical evidence for short implants versus augmentation.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Evidence-Based Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Builds the critical-appraisal skills needed to distinguish reliable clinical evidence from opinion and apply research findings to implant decisions.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Evidence-Based Implant Dentistry
materials.summary: Covers study design, levels of evidence, randomisation, blinding, outcomes, meta-analysis and practical appraisal of implant literature.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Evidence and Critical Appraisal
materials.summary: Tests study design, evidence hierarchy, blinding, dropouts, outcome selection and interpretation of the clinical literature.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Peri-Implant Disease: Diagnosis and Management
lectures.copy: Explores the diagnosis, prevalence, risk factors and evidence-informed management of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Peri-Implant Disease
materials.summary: Reviews aetiology, probing, radiographic interpretation, implant surfaces, prevalence, risk factors and current treatment evidence.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Peri-Implant Disease
materials.summary: Checks diagnosis, aetiology, probing findings, implant surfaces, prevalence data and evidence-based management principles.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Short Implants, Augmentation and Peri-Implant Health
lectures.copy: Compares short implants with augmentation for posterior ridge cases and connects implant design, complications and long-term peri-implant health.

materials.label: Lecture 3: Short Implants, Augmentation and Peri-Implant Health
materials.summary: Uses comparative evidence to examine short implants, sinus augmentation, morbidity, implant design, complications and maintenance of peri-implant health.

materials.label: Quiz 3: Short Implants and Peri-Implant Health
materials.summary: Assesses short-implant selection, sinus and ridge augmentation evidence, complications, biomechanics and peri-implant health.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Implant timing and clinical decision-making day covering the ITI placement classification, grafting choices, primary stability and loading protocols.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Timing of Implant Placement and the ITI Classification
lectures.copy: Explains how biological tissue state, rather than the calendar alone, guides immediate, early and delayed implant placement decisions.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Timing of Implant Placement and the ITI Classification
materials.summary: Covers the evidence behind implant timing, healing milestones, the ITI Types 1–4 classification and how each tissue state shapes treatment planning.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Timing and the ITI Classification
materials.summary: Tests immediate, early and delayed placement concepts, healing states, evidence interpretation and application of ITI Types 1–4.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Clinical Decision-Making, Grafting and Loading
lectures.copy: Turns implant timing classifications into practical chairside decisions about immediate placement, grafting, stability, loading and guided surgery.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Clinical Decision-Making, Grafting and Loading
materials.summary: Covers immediate-placement selection, jumping-gap management, socket grafting, insertion torque, loading thresholds and guided implant placement.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Decision-Making, Grafting and Loading
materials.summary: Assesses immediate-placement risks, grafting choices, jumping-gap protocols, torque thresholds, loading decisions and guided surgery.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Dental photography day showing how clinical images support diagnosis, communication, planning and case documentation.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Implant Dentistry Photography Basics
lectures.copy: Introduces camera setup, mirrors, retractors and standard views for consistent clinical records.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Photography for Planning and Communication
lectures.copy: Shows how images support aesthetic assessment, patient discussions, lab communication and multidisciplinary planning.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Documentation and Portfolio Standards
lectures.copy: Covers image organisation, consent, case presentation and the photographic standards expected in implant training.

modules.title: Module 5
modules.topics: Treatment Planning, Case Readiness, Surgical Protocols and Placement-Day Workflow for Course Patients.

days.title: Clinical Weekend
days.copy: Two-lecture clinical weekend focused on moving safely from case readiness into supervised implant placement and post-operative discharge.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Treatment Planning and Case Readiness
lectures.copy: Clarifies the first-case mindset, mentor sign-off, diagnostic readiness and the checks needed before a patient becomes a safe surgical case.

materials.label: Lecture 1: Treatment Planning and Case Readiness
materials.summary: Covers patient suitability, risk screening, diagnostics, consent, mentor review, digital readiness and the habits that make first implant cases controlled and defensible.

materials.label: Quiz 1: Treatment Planning
materials.summary: Tests case-readiness checks, planning risk, patient communication, diagnostic records, consent and mentor-review principles.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Surgical Protocol and Placement Day
lectures.copy: Takes the approved plan into surgery, with a practical workflow for setup, sterile discipline, mentor checkpoints and post-operative discharge.

materials.label: Lecture 2: Surgical Protocol and Placement Day
materials.summary: Reviews placement-day preparation, surgical sequencing, sterility, drilling and placement checks, decision language, immediate complications and discharge instructions.

materials.label: Quiz 2: Surgical Protocol
materials.summary: Checks surgical setup, sterile workflow, mentor checkpoint language, placement-day decisions, post-operative instructions and early complication awareness.

modules.title: Module 6
modules.topics: Medico-legal Considerations, Prosthetic Principles in Implant Dentistry, Impressions and Temporisation in Implant Dentistry.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Medico-legal foundations day covering consent, records, complaints prevention and professional decision-making in implant dentistry.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Medico-Legal Principles in Implant Care
lectures.copy: Reviews duty of care, consent, scope of practice, record keeping and the common preventable causes of complaints.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Documentation and Risk Communication
lectures.copy: Focuses on writing records that show diagnosis, options, risks, consent and patient-specific decision-making.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Managing Complaints and Complications
lectures.copy: Explains how to communicate after complications, handle dissatisfaction and protect the patient relationship.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Prosthetic principles day covering implant restoration design, component choice and the mechanics of long-term function.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Prosthetic Principles in Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Introduces restoration-led planning, emergence profile, component selection and the differences between teeth and implants.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Screw-Retained and Cement-Retained Options
lectures.copy: Compares retention choices, retrievability, complication risks and design decisions for implant restorations.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Prosthetic Complications and Maintenance
lectures.copy: Covers screw loosening, ceramic fracture, peri-implant tissue issues and maintenance planning.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Impressions and temporisation day focused on capturing implant position accurately and protecting tissues during restorative phases.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Implant Impressions
lectures.copy: Covers open-tray and closed-tray approaches, impression copings, verification and sources of inaccuracy.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Temporisation in Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Explains provisional restoration design, tissue shaping, aesthetics and occlusal control during healing.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · From Impression to Definitive Restoration
lectures.copy: Links records, lab communication, try-in checks and delivery steps for predictable final restorations.

modules.title: Module 7
modules.topics: Advanced Prosthetic Principles and Impressions in Implant Dentistry, and Occlusion in Implant Dentistry.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Advanced prosthetic planning day focused on complex restorative design, occlusion and long-term biomechanical stability.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Advanced Prosthetic Planning
lectures.copy: Develops restoration-led thinking for complex implant cases, including space, aesthetics, cleansability and component strategy.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Occlusion in Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Explains occlusal risk, force direction, parafunction and how implant restorations should be adjusted for protection.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Biomechanics of Complex Restorations
lectures.copy: Covers span length, cantilevers, splinting, screw mechanics and design features that reduce mechanical complications.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Advanced impression and verification day covering accuracy, fit and communication for more demanding implant restorations.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Advanced Implant Impressions
lectures.copy: Reviews impression accuracy for multiple implants, verification jigs and techniques for reducing distortion.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Try-In, Fit and Passive Seating
lectures.copy: Focuses on framework fit, radiographic checks, screw tests and when to remake records before delivery.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Laboratory Communication for Complex Cases
lectures.copy: Covers prescription quality, shade and tissue communication, digital records and avoiding avoidable lab-stage errors.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Occlusion and maintenance integration day for protecting advanced implant prostheses over time.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Occlusal Assessment and Adjustment
lectures.copy: Covers records, articulator planning, contact design and chairside adjustment for implant restorations.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Managing Mechanical Complications
lectures.copy: Explains prevention and management of screw loosening, prosthetic fracture, wear and occlusal overload.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Maintenance for Advanced Prosthetics
lectures.copy: Sets out recall, hygiene, occlusal review and repair pathways for complex implant-supported restorations.

modules.title: Module 8
modules.topics: Digital Workflow in Implant Dentistry, Soft Tissue Grafting (FGG, CTG) and Fitting Final Restorations for Course Implant Patients.

days.title: Day 1
days.copy: Digital workflow day covering scan acquisition, planning software, guided surgery and digital communication.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Digital Workflow in Implant Dentistry
lectures.copy: Introduces intraoral scanning, CBCT integration, digital planning and how digital records support diagnosis and treatment.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Guided Surgery and Digital Planning
lectures.copy: Explains guide design, prosthetically driven planning, accuracy limits and when guided surgery adds value.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Digital Communication and Records
lectures.copy: Covers file transfer, lab collaboration, patient communication and maintaining clean digital documentation.

days.title: Day 2
days.copy: Soft tissue grafting day focused on free gingival grafts, connective tissue grafts and peri-implant tissue quality.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Soft Tissue Grafting Principles
lectures.copy: Reviews keratinised tissue, mucosal thickness, graft biology and indications for peri-implant soft tissue augmentation.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Free Gingival Grafts and Connective Tissue Grafts
lectures.copy: Compares FGG and CTG techniques, donor-site considerations, handling and expected clinical outcomes.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Aesthetic Tissue Management
lectures.copy: Focuses on emergence profile, tissue volume, recession prevention and soft tissue decisions in the aesthetic zone.

days.title: Day 3
days.copy: Final restoration day for course implant patients, covering fit, occlusion, delivery and maintenance instructions.

lectures.title: Lecture 1 · Fitting Final Restorations
lectures.copy: Covers clinical checks, radiographs, torque protocols, contacts, occlusion and final delivery of implant restorations.

lectures.title: Lecture 2 · Patient Instructions and Maintenance
lectures.copy: Explains hygiene instruction, review intervals, complication warning signs and long-term maintenance planning.

lectures.title: Lecture 3 · Course Case Completion Review
